key_concepts: Carrying capacity is the maximum population size an ecosystem can maintain.
Limiting factors are environmental conditions or resources that restrict population growth
Limiting factors may be density-dependent or density-independent.
Food, water, shelter, space, oxygen, and mates are examples of limiting factors.
Abiotic and biotic factors determine how many organisms an ecosystem can support.
Decomposers recycle dead organisms and organic matter, preventing accumulation and affecti
Population growth slows as it reaches carrying capacity, producing logistic growth.
Exponential growth occurs when resources are unlimited.
Natural disasters can destroy resources and decrease carrying capacity.
Humans can alter carrying capacity by manipulating natural resources.
